uncited: It builds on [Tensor Times Matrix (TTM) Reconstruction](7404-tensor-times-matrix-ttm-reconstruction.md) by optimizing the sequential application of TTM kernels for the Tucker decomposition model.

It sets itself apart from [Partial Decoding](14061-partial-decoding.md) by focusing on the algebraic rearrangement of the full summation to minimize floating-point operations rather than skipping data blocks.
*   Core tensor $B$ of size $R_1 \times R_2 \times R_3$.
Permute the modes such that the first mode index $r$ corresponds to the smallest rank $R_1$.
**Inner Loop (Mode 3):** Compute the weighted sum of the third basis matrix columns scaled by the core tensor entries.
More precisely, for fixed $r, s$, $V_{r,s}$ is the linear combination of the columns of $U^{(3)}$ weighted by $B[r, s, :]$.
**Middle Loop (Mode 2):** Compute the outer product accumulation.
Here, $U^{(2)}[:, s]$ is the $s$-th column of $U^{(2)}$.
The outer product $u \otimes v$ creates a matrix where $M_r[i, j] = u[i] \cdot v[j]$.
This adds the outer product of the $r$-th column of $U^{(1)}$ and the matrix $M_r$ to the global accumulator $A_f$.
*   Typical values: Ranks are chosen based on visual accuracy or error thresholds.
*   **Memory:** The intermediate storage for $V_{r,s}$ and $M_r$ must fit in cache or local memory to avoid bandwidth bottlenecks. $M_r$ requires $I_2 \cdot I_3$ space.
*   **Degenerate Input:** If any $R_k = 0$, the output is zero.
**Limitations:** Requires the tensor decomposition to be pre-computed.
